Author: R.Mala
Bench: R.Mala
Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court 
Dated: 12.10.2015 
Coram 
The Honourable Ms.Justice R.Mala 
CRL.O.P.(MD).No.8264 of 2009 
and 
M.P.(MD)No.1 of 2009 
S.R.Moorthy : Petitioner
Vs.
Food Inspector,
Nagercoil Municipality,
Nagercoil. : Respondent

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code
praying to call for the records relating to the complaint in S.T.C.No.76 of
2006, dated 12.07.2006 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate No.II,
Nagercoil and quash the proceedings.
For Petitioner : Mr.C.Ramachandran 
For Respondent : Mr.P.Kannithevan, 
 Government Advocate (Criminal Side) 
:O R D E R
The quash petition has been filed by the petitioner seeking to quash the complaint in S.T.C.No.76 of 2006, dated 12.07.2006 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Nagercoil.
2. Heard both sides.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner, who is the second accused, has come forward with this petition to quash the proceedings in S.T.C.No.76 of 2006,
stating that the respondent herein has taken sample on 29.04.2003 and after following the procedures, that has been sent for analysis and report has been received on 04.06.2003, in which, it S.R.Moorthy vs Food Inspector on 12 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116023543/
1 was stated that sample was misbranded, since it did not contain the word 'synthetic food colour' in capital letters on the label of the food sample and as per Rule 24 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, the addition of colouring matters shall be declared on the label in capital letters as it contains permitted "SYNTHETIC FOOD COLOURS".

Further, since the label of the sample contains the word only "contains permitted Class II Preservatives permitted colour and added flavours FPO 1965/1", there is a contravention of the provisions of Rule 24.
On receipt of analyst report, the respondent preferred a complaint on 12.07.2006 and the same has been taken on file as S.T.C.No.76 of 2006 by the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Nagercoil.

He received a copy of summons on 12.07.2006 and as such, his right under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954,
to send the sample for second analysis has been curtailed.
Hence, due to inordinate delay in launching the complaint on the part of the prosecuting agency, valuable right of the accused has been taken away.
Hence, he prayed for quashing the complaint.

4. Adding further, the learned counsel would submit that in the bottle, it was specifically mentioned as 'Mfg.Date: March, 2003, Best Before 6 months from the date of manufacturing' and the complaint was preferred only on 12.07.2006 and as such, it is barred by limitation.

To substantiate his argument, he relied upon the judgments reported in 2005-2-LW (Crl.) 598 [C.Suresh & others v.
The State, etc.] and 2008 (3) MLJ (Crl.) 779 [Baskar Vembu v. State of Tamil Nadu].
5.

entities.text: 2008 (3) MLJ (Crl.) 779 [Baskar Vembu v. State of Tamil Nadu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel would further submit that as per Section 468 Cr.P.C., it is barred by limitation, because the maximum punishment provided for misbranding is not exceeding 3 years imprisonment.
For all these reasons, he prayed for quashing the complaint.

6. The learned Government Advocate (Criminal side) would submit that as per the report dated 04.06.2003, the sample was misbranded and as such, complaint has been preferred on 12.07.2006 and the same has been taken on file as S.T.C.No.76 of 2006.

7. I have considered the submissions made on both sides and perused the typed-set of papers, which shows that on 29.04.2003 at 10.40 a.m., sample has been taken and the same has been sent for food analysis and report has been received on 04.06.2003, wherein it was stated that the sample was misbranded and the petitioner received the summons on 12.07.2006 and the complaint has been given only on 12.07.2006 i.e., after three years.
8. As per Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the maximum punishment for the offences alleged is 3 years and fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees.
However, in the case on hand, complaint has been filed after three years.

9. At this juncture, it is useful to extract Section 468 Cr.P.C., which reads thus:
"Bar to taking cognizance after lapse of the period of limitation.-

(1) Except as otherwise provided elsewhere in this Code, no Court shall take cognizance of an offence of the category specified in sub-section (2), after the expiry of the period of limitation.
S.R.Moorthy vs Food Inspector on 12 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116023543/
2
(2) The period of limitation shall be- (a) six months, if the offence is punishable with fine only;

(b) one year, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year;
(c) three years, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding one year but not exceeding three years.

(3) for the purposes of this section, the period of limitation, in relation to offences which may be tried together, shall be determined with reference to the offence which is punishable with the more severe punishment or, as the case may be, the most severe punishment."

10. Therefore, as per Section 468(2)(c) Cr.P.C., three years, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding one year but not exceeding three years, I am of the view that in the case on hand, the complaint has been filed only on 12.07.2006 i.e., after a period of three years and as such, it is barred by limitation.
11.

Applying the decisions of this Court in 2005-2-LW (Crl.) 598 [C.Suresh & others v. The State,
etc.] and 2008 (3) MLJ (Crl.) 779 [Baskar Vembu v. State of Tamil Nadu] to the case on hand, I am of the view that the valuable right provided under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, to send the sample for second analysis, has been taken away, since the prosecution has been levied after lapse of time.

entities.text: 2008 (3) MLJ (Crl.) 779 [Baskar Vembu v. State of Tamil Nadu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. For the reasons stated above, the petition is allowed and the complaint in S.T.C.No.76 of 2006,
dated 12.07.2006 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Nagercoil, in respect of the petitioner alone, is hereby quashed.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
To 1.The Judicial Magistrate No.II, Nagercoil.
2.The Food Inspector, Nagercoil Municipality, Nagercoil.
3.The Additional Public Prosecutor, Madurai Bench of Madras High Court, Madurai.
